problem.title: Turnaround Time from Kit Ship to Result
problem.prompt: You are analyzing an at-home diagnostic test kit platform. The `kit_shipments` table tracks when each kit was shipped to a customer and when the lab released the result, modeled after CDC surveillance datasets for at-home testing programs. Each kit has a `customer_id` (stored as TEXT but always numeric), a `ship_date` (DATE), a `result_released_at` (TIMESTAMP), a `test_type` code (stored in a TEXT[] array where the first element is the primary test code), and a `customer_name` (TEXT that may have inconsistent casing and whitespace). Calculate the turnaround time in hours from ship to result release for each customer. For customers who received multiple kits, compute the average turnaround in hours, rounded to one decimal place. Only include customers whose average turnaround is 72 hours or more. Return `customer_id` (as an INTEGER), `customer_name` (trimmed and title-cased), `primary_test_code` (the first element of the test_type array), `ship_month` (the month of their first shipment, formatted as 'YYYY-MM'), and `avg_turnaround_hours` (NUMERIC rounded to one decimal). Order by `avg_turnaround_hours` descending, then by `customer_id` ascending.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE kit_shipments (shipment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id TEXT, customer_name TEXT, ship_date DATE, result_released_at TIMESTAMP, test_type TEXT[]);

composite_moves: extract test_type[1] array element for primary code
compute EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (result_released_at - ship_date)) / 3600 for turnaround hours per shipment
group by customer_id with AVG turnaround and MIN ship_date for first shipment month
TRIM and INITCAP customer_name for consistent casing
order by avg_turnaround_hours DESC, customer_id ASC

hints: You need to compute the time difference between two timestamp columns and convert it to hours. Group by customer to find the average.
Use EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (timestamp2 - timestamp1)) / 3600 to get hours. The customer_id column is text, so cast it to INTEGER. The test_type column is an array; access the first element with [1].

GROUP BY customer_id::INTEGER. Calculate AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (result_released_at - ship_date)) / 3600) and apply HAVING to filter >= 72 hours. Use DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(ship_date)) for the first ship month, format with TO_CHAR(..., 'YYYY-MM'). Clean customer_name with INITCAP(TRIM(...)). Access test_type[1] for primary code. ROUND the average to 1 decimal.
problem.answer_key: SELECT customer_id::INTEGER, INITCAP(TRIM(customer_name)) AS customer_name, test_type[1] AS primary_test_code, TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(ship_date)), 'YYYY-MM') AS ship_month, ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (result_released_at - ship_date)) / 3600), 1) AS avg_turnaround_hours FROM kit_shipments GROUP BY customer_id::INTEGER, INITCAP(TRIM(customer_name)), test_type[1] HAVING AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (result_released_at - ship_date)) / 3600) >= 72 ORDER BY avg_turnaround_hours DESC, customer_id::INTEGER ASC;

_meta.scenario: an at-home diagnostic test kit platform tracking kit shipped and results released

user_solution:
/*
You are analyzing an at-home diagnostic test kit platform.


Table: kit_shipments    tracks when each kit was shipped to a customer and when the lab released the result
shipment_id	            INT PRIMARY KEY
customer_id	            TEXT
customer_name	        TEXT
ship_date	            DATE
result_released_at	    TIMESTAMP
test_type	            TEXT[]        first element is the primary test code


PURPOSE:
- Calculate the turnaround time in hours from ship to result release for each customer.
- For customers who received multiple kits, compute the average turnaround in hours, rounded to one decimal place.
- Only include customers whose average turnaround is 72 hours or more.

OUTPUT
customer_id                INT
customer_name              (trimmed and title-cased), 
primary_test_code          (the first element of the test_type array), 
ship_month                 (the month of their first shipment, formatted as 'YYYY-MM'), and 
avg_turnaround_hours       (NUMERIC rounded to one decimal).



STEPS
1. DATA CLEANING
2. CAL TURN AROUND TIME
3. GROUP BY AND VG
4. HAVING FILTER
*/
WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id::int,
        INITCAP(TRIM(customer_name)) AS customer_name,
        test_type[1] AS primary_test_code,
        TO_CHAR(ship_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS ship_month,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH from (result_released_at::timestamp - ship_date::timestamp)) /3600 AS turnaround_hours
    FROM kit_shipments
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    customer_name,
    primary_test_code,
    MIN(ship_month) AS ship_month,
    ROUND(AVG(turnaround_hours),1) AS avg_turnaround_hours
FROM base
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING ROUND(AVG(turnaround_hours::numeric),1) >= 72
ORDER BY avg_turnaround_hours DESC, customer_id ASC;
